events.subtitle: NYC / DMV improvisational exchange — guitar, vibraphone, trombone and tenor saxophone
lineup: Selendis S. A. Johnson — vibraphone, trombone
events.factual_description: Transparent Production presents Pérez / Johnson / Dougherty / Dixon at Rhizome DC on Wednesday, September 30, 2026. Doors are at 18:30 and music begins at 19:00 at 6950 Maple Street NW, Washington, DC. Rhizome and its authorized Pools ticket page list a $20-$30 sliding-scale ticket; Pools separately displays fee-inclusive totals of $22.47-$33.02. The primary venue page describes an evening of improvisations with NYC-based Gían Pérez on guitar and Selendis S. A. Johnson on vibraphone and trombone, in duo and solo performance with the DMV duo of Nelson Dougherty on guitar and Zach Dixon on tenor saxophone. Rhizome identifies Pérez as a Puerto Rico-born, Brooklyn-based artist, improviser and composer who extends the electric guitar toward its physical extremes; Johnson as a vibraphonist and trombonist working in Black-American improvisation-based music; Dougherty as a Washington, DC guitarist who uses pedals to create expansive soundscapes; and Dixon as a saxophonist, composer and improviser working across experimental and narrative forms. The source does not specify a detailed set order beyond the stated duo/solo framing, so none is inferred.

en.why_it_matters: The draw is the instrumental collision. Pérez treats electric guitar as raw physical material rather than a fixed jazz or rock voice; Johnson moves between vibraphone and trombone inside Black-American improvisational practice; Dougherty brings pedal-built guitar soundscapes from the DMV; and Dixon answers with tenor saxophone and a narrative, experimental ear. The NYC-to-DC exchange gives the night a live reason of its own: four players using familiar instruments as unstable material rather than simply sharing a bill.
en.trip_verdict: If Wednesday is free in the DMV, this is worth catching at Rhizome for the improvisational and instrumental thread. It is a local discovery to fold into the week, not a reason to build a separate regional trip.

es.why_it_matters: Lo atractivo está en el choque instrumental. Pérez trata la guitarra eléctrica como materia física antes que como una voz fija de jazz o rock; Johnson se mueve entre vibráfono y trombón dentro de la improvisación afroamericana; Dougherty trae desde el DMV sus paisajes de guitarra construidos con pedales; y Dixon responde con sax tenor y un oído narrativo y experimental. El cruce Nueva York-DC le da a la noche una razón propia: cuatro músicos usando instrumentos conocidos como material inestable, no simplemente compartiendo cartel.
es.trip_verdict: Si el miércoles está libre en el DMV, vale caer a Rhizome por el hilo improvisatorio e instrumental. Es un descubrimiento local para incorporar a la semana, no una razón para armar un viaje regional aparte.
